title: Saving for Goals
blurb: Turn "I want it" into a plan with a date.
cards: i
Goals need a number and a date
"Save more" is a wish. "Save 600 for a laptop by June" is a plan. Divide the target by the months left to get your monthly amount.
q
You want 600 in 6 months. How much do you save each month?
600 ÷ 6 = 100 per month.
i
Where to keep savings
Keep goal money separate from spending, ideally in a savings account that pays interest. Out of sight means less temptation to dip into it.
t
Interest means your savings can grow without you adding anything.
Savings accounts pay interest, so your balance grows slowly over time.
i
Small steps compound
Money that earns interest then earns interest on that interest. That is compounding, and it rewards starting early far more than saving big amounts later.
q
Why does starting to save early matter so much?
Banks give young people bonuses
Time lets interest build on interest
Prices never rise
It does not matter
Compounding needs time. The earlier you start, the longer it works for you.
q
Which habit best protects a savings goal?
Moving the money automatically on payday
Saving whatever is left at month end
Keeping it in your spending account
Telling nobody
Automatic transfers remove willpower from the equation.
example: A $480 laptop goal is eight months away. Saving $60 each month reaches the target before any changes in price or interest.
